answer.answer: NVIDIA states that as of the end of fiscal year 2026 it was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center compute market, because under current rules it cannot create and deliver a product approved by both the USG and the Chinese government [1][2]. The company says export controls have also negatively impacted demand for its products in other markets, such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [3]. Export restrictions targeting China were announced in August 2022 and expanded in October 2023, with licensing requirements covering products such as the A100, H100, and B200 [4]. The Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged purchases of NVIDIA data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [5][6]. Under the new H200 licensing program, shipments must go through an inspection process in the United States, and any H200 shipped under the program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States [1].
